transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, thank you. I guess I came in because for the past few weeks I’ve just felt this really heavy sadness, like a pressure sitting on me almost all day. It’s hard to explain without sounding dramatic, but it feels like I’m carrying something around constantly.

I’m still going to work and doing what I’m supposed to do — I’m a nurse, so I’m used to putting on a pleasant face and smiling with patients — but inside I feel like I’m barely keeping it together. Like I can look normal on the outside, but underneath I feel really sad and weighed down most of the day.
Did this sadness start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?

Um… yeah, I think it did kind of start after something specific. It’s been about three weeks now, maybe a little over, and it was shortly after I found out I was pregnant.

I don’t know if I can say it was exactly that moment, like a switch flipped, but looking back the timing is pretty close. I found out, and then not long after that this sadness just sort of settled in and hasn’t really lifted. It’s been there most days since then.
Does this sadness feel mainly like a reaction to finding out you’re pregnant?

I mean… maybe partly, yeah. The timing lines up so closely that it’s hard not to connect the two. It’s been about three weeks, starting not long after I found out I was pregnant, and since then the sadness has just kind of stayed there.

I don’t know if it’s only because of the pregnancy, or if finding out just brought something up in me, but that’s when I really noticed it starting. It wasn’t like I felt this way for months before and then happened to find out — it really began shortly after that.
Does finding out you’re pregnant feel like the main reason you’ve been feeling this way?

I’m not completely sure, honestly. It’s the thing I keep circling back to because the timing is so close, so part of me feels like… maybe, yes, it has something to do with it. But I don’t know that I can say it’s the main reason with confidence.

It’s more like finding out I’m pregnant happened, and then this heavy feeling came in afterward, and now I’m trying to make sense of it. I keep asking myself, “Is this because of the pregnancy? Is it fear? Is it something else?” And I don’t really have a clean answer. It feels connected, but I can’t tell whether it’s the whole cause or just what made me notice how bad I was feeling.
Before this started three weeks ago, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this?

I… I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think I’ve had anything that felt exactly like this before, at least not that I can clearly point to.

I’ve had stressful times, of course, and times where I felt down or overwhelmed, but this feels different enough that I’m hesitant to say, “Yes, this happened before.” I’m trying to think back, and nothing is really standing out to me as a period where I felt this same kind of sadness for days and days like this. So… I guess my answer is no, not that I can remember.
Do you feel that the pregnancy is what’s causing this sadness?

I don’t know if I can say that for sure. It feels connected, because it started around the same time, and that makes it really hard for me not to link the two in my head. But saying, “Yes, the pregnancy is causing this,” feels too definite, and I don’t feel that certain.

It’s more like… I found out, and then afterward this sadness was there, and now I keep trying to figure out whether one caused the other or whether it just brought something to the surface. I wish I had a clearer answer, but I really don’t. It feels related, but I can’t honestly say I know it’s the cause.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes… I think I have. That’s actually been one of the things that feels really unlike me.

After my shifts, I used to have things I’d do to sort of come back to myself, you know? Like I would paint sometimes, even if it was just something small, or I’d go to yoga, or salsa class if I had the energy. Those were the things that usually helped me decompress after work and made me feel like I wasn’t just working and sleeping.

But lately I just… don’t. I go home, sit on the couch, and everything feels like too much effort. Even when I think, “Maybe I should go to yoga,” it doesn’t feel appealing the way it used to. It feels like a chore before I even start. And I’ve been ignoring texts too, not because I’m mad at anyone, but because responding or making plans just feels like more than I can do, and none of it feels worth it right now.
Before these past three weeks, had you been feeling depressed or down most days for at least two years?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I was stressed or tired or just not feeling great, especially with work and life stuff, but not depressed or down most days for two years.

That sounds like… a really long, ongoing thing, and I don’t think that was me before these last few weeks. I’m trying to be careful because I don’t want to say something too quickly, but when I think back over the past couple years, I wouldn’t describe myself as feeling like this most days. This feels much more recent.
How much of your sadness feels directly tied to thinking about the pregnancy?

A lot of it feels tied to it, honestly… but not in a neat, direct way where every time I think about the pregnancy, I get sad, and if I don’t think about it, I’m fine. It’s more like since finding out, this heaviness has been sitting on me almost all day.

I came in because for the past few weeks I’ve felt this heavy, sad pressure on me, like it’s just there in the background no matter what I’m doing. Even at work, I can be smiling at patients and doing what I’m supposed to do, and from the outside I probably look okay, but inside I feel like I’m barely holding myself together.

So when I think about the pregnancy, yes, it can make that feeling sharper or more real, I guess. But the sadness doesn’t completely switch off when I’m not actively thinking about it. It kind of follows me around.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes… definitely. That’s been happening a lot, and it’s honestly scaring me a little because at work I’m usually very careful and pretty quick with routine things.

Lately my brain just feels foggy, like I’m trying to think through cotton or something. I’ll read a medication order and then realize I didn’t actually take it in, so I read it again… and then sometimes again, because I don’t trust that I understood it the first time. Same with wound-care notes. I’ll be standing there looking at them, and it’s not that I can’t read them, obviously, but it’s like the information doesn’t stick the way it normally does.

And decisions that I normally make almost automatically now make me freeze. Like I’ll know what I’m supposed to do, but then I start second-guessing myself — “Did I read that right? Am I remembering the dressing change correctly? Should I check again?” It takes me longer than it should, and I feel really frustrated with myself because I’m used to being competent and steady with that kind of thing.
Does the intensity of this sadness feel stronger than you would expect just from finding out you’re pregnant?

Yes… I think so. I keep asking myself that, like, “Is this just because I found out I’m pregnant? Is this a normal reaction?” And I know that’s a big thing to take in, so I don’t want to make it sound like it has nothing to do with it.

But the level of sadness feels… bigger than that, I guess. Heavier. It’s not just a moment of being upset or overwhelmed when I think about it. For the past few weeks it’s felt like this heavy, sad pressure just sitting on me almost all day. Like it follows me around.

Even when I’m at work and I’m smiling at patients and doing what I’m supposed to be doing, inside I feel like I’m barely holding myself together. So yes, I’d say it feels stronger than what I would expect from just finding out. It feels like it’s taken over more of me than that.
Do you feel sad most of the day nearly every day, even when you’re not thinking about the pregnancy?

Yes… most of the day, nearly every day. It’s not just when I’m actively thinking about the pregnancy. That can definitely bring it up more sharply, but even when my mind is on something else, there’s still this heavy, sad pressure sitting on me.

That’s really why I came in, because for the past few weeks it’s felt like it’s there almost all day. I’ll be at work, smiling at patients, answering questions, doing what I’m supposed to do, and I think from the outside I probably look normal enough. But inside I feel like I’m barely holding myself together. It’s like I’m carrying this weight around while trying to act like everything is fine.
Have you noticed any change in your sleep?

I’m not totally sure, honestly. I haven’t been tracking my sleep closely enough to give you a clear answer, and I don’t want to say there’s been a definite change if I’m just guessing.

It hasn’t stood out to me as the main thing, I guess. Like, when I think about what’s been feeling wrong, sleep isn’t the first thing that comes to mind. But I also haven’t really stopped and paid attention to whether it’s different from my normal. So… I’d say I’m not sure.
Have you been feeling worthless or unusually guilty lately?

I don’t know… I’ve been trying to sort that out, because “worthless” feels like a really strong word. I don’t know that I would say I feel worthless exactly.

I do feel… disappointed in myself sometimes, or like I should be handling things better than I am. Like I’ll catch myself thinking, “You’re a nurse, you take care of other people, you’re supposed to be able to keep it together,” and then I feel bad that I can’t just push through it. But I’m not sure if that’s guilt in the way you mean it.

It’s more like I’m judging myself, I guess. Like I should be stronger or more grateful or more clear-headed. But I haven’t really thought of it as, like, “I’m a worthless person.” It’s just… I don’t feel like myself, and then I feel bad about not feeling like myself.
Have these feelings made it hard for you to do your job or manage your usual responsibilities?

Yes… I think it has, even though I’m still showing up and doing my shifts. I haven’t called out or anything, and I keep telling myself that means I’m functioning, but it’s not the same as before.

At work, I’m getting through the day, but it takes so much more effort to stay on top of everything. My supervisor has already noticed that some of my charting hasn’t been finished the way it should be, which felt really embarrassing. I’m usually very careful about that, so having someone point it out made me feel like, okay, this isn’t just in my head. It’s actually affecting how I’m doing my job.

And outside of work, I’ve been pulling back a lot. Friends will text me and I’ll see it and think I should answer, and then I just… don’t. Or I put it off until it feels too awkward. I’m also not really doing the things that usually keep me steady, like staying connected with people or keeping up with my normal routines. I still manage the basic responsibilities, but it feels like I’m doing the bare minimum and slowly letting the rest slip.
Have you had any thoughts about wanting to die or hurting yourself?

Yeah… um… that’s actually the thing that scared me enough to say something at my prenatal appointment.

I haven’t made a plan to hurt myself, and I don’t have, like, a specific thing I’m going to do. But I’ve been having thoughts like… I wish I could just not wake up. Like if I went to sleep and somehow didn’t have to keep doing this, there’s a part of me that feels relieved by that thought, and that really scared me when I noticed it.

It’s hard to say out loud because I don’t want people to think I’m trying to do something or that I’m unsafe every second, but it also doesn’t feel okay to keep pretending it’s nothing. I haven’t been thinking, “I’m going to hurt myself,” exactly. It’s more like I don’t want to be here, or I want everything to stop, and then I feel awful and frightened that I’m even thinking that.
Have you noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking more slowly than usual lately?

Yeah… I think so. I didn’t really have words for it at first, but it feels like everything I do is slowed down, like I’m moving through syrup or something. Not just tired, exactly, but like my body takes longer to start and longer to finish anything.

At the clinic, even simple things that I normally do automatically feel like they take effort. Like gathering wound care supplies — that should be quick, I know where everything is — but I’ll find myself moving so slowly, double-checking, standing there for a second like I’m trying to remember the next step. And charting takes me noticeably longer than it should. I’ll be sitting there trying to finish something that used to feel routine, and it’s like my hands and my brain are both dragging.

I don’t know if other people would see it as me moving in slow motion or if it just feels that way to me, but I definitely notice that I’m not as quick or efficient as I usually am. It’s frustrating because I know how I normally function, and this is not that.
When you’re occupied with something unrelated to the pregnancy, does the sadness still feel just as strong?

Yeah… it does. That’s part of what’s been confusing and honestly kind of scary to me. It’s not only when I’m thinking about the pregnancy or appointments or anything like that. Even when I’m busy with something completely separate, like work stuff, talking to a patient, trying to chart, or doing something that should distract me, it’s still there.

I can be smiling at a patient and saying the right things, and on the outside I probably look normal enough, but inside it feels like there’s this heavy, sad pressure just sitting on me almost all day. Like I’m having to hold myself together underneath everything I’m doing. Sometimes I’ll realize I’ve been going through the motions for hours, and the sadness hasn’t really lifted — I’ve just been trying to work around it.

That’s honestly why I came in. It’s been going on for the past few weeks, and it feels like it follows me into whatever I’m doing, not just when I’m focused on one specific worry.

But the level of sadness feels… bigger than that, I guess. Heavier. It’s not just a moment of being upset or overwhelmed when I think about it. For the past few weeks it’s felt like this heavy, sad pressure just sitting on me almost all day. Like it follows me around.

Even when I’m at work and I’m smiling at patients and doing what I’m supposed to be doing, inside I feel like I’m barely holding myself together. So yes, I’d say it feels stronger than what I would expect from just finding out. It feels like it’s taken over more of me than that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the symptoms are occurring beyond what would be expected as a stress reaction, favoring major depressive episode over adjustment disorder.
doctor.question: Do you feel sad most of the day nearly every day, even when you’re not thinking about the pregnancy?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: I came in because for the past few weeks I’ve felt this heavy, sad pressure sitting on me almost all day, and even when I’m at work smiling at patients, inside I feel like I’m barely holding myself together.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking whether sadness persists most of the day nearly every day, independent of thoughts about the pregnancy, which corresponds to depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yes… most of the day, nearly every day. It’s not just when I’m actively thinking about the pregnancy. That can definitely bring it up more sharply, but even when my mind is on something else, there’s still this heavy, sad pressure sitting on me.

That’s really why I came in, because for the past few weeks it’s felt like it’s there almost all day. I’ll be at work, smiling at patients, answering questions, doing what I’m supposed to do, and I think from the outside I probably look normal enough. But inside I feel like I’m barely holding myself together. It’s like I’m carrying this weight around while trying to act like everything is fine.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are neurovegetative changes consistent with a major depressive episode rather than an adjustment disorder.
doctor.question: Have you noticed any change in your sleep?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about sleep changes, but the provided symptom profile does not include a sleep-related symptom item.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure, honestly. I haven’t been tracking my sleep closely enough to give you a clear answer, and I don’t want to say there’s been a definite change if I’m just guessing.

It hasn’t stood out to me as the main thing, I guess. Like, when I think about what’s been feeling wrong, sleep isn’t the first thing that comes to mind. But I also haven’t really stopped and paid attention to whether it’s different from my normal. So… I’d say I’m not sure.

doctor.intent: Determine whether she has worthlessness or excessive guilt, a key major depressive episode symptom that would help distinguish major depressive disorder from adjustment disorder.
doctor.question: Have you been feeling worthless or unusually guilty lately?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of worthlessness or excessive/unusual guilt, but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific item covering guilt or worthlessness.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… I’ve been trying to sort that out, because “worthless” feels like a really strong word. I don’t know that I would say I feel worthless exactly.

I do feel… disappointed in myself sometimes, or like I should be handling things better than I am. Like I’ll catch myself thinking, “You’re a nurse, you take care of other people, you’re supposed to be able to keep it together,” and then I feel bad that I can’t just push through it. But I’m not sure if that’s guilt in the way you mean it.

It’s more like I’m judging myself, I guess. Like I should be stronger or more grateful or more clear-headed. But I haven’t really thought of it as, like, “I’m a worthless person.” It’s just… I don’t feel like myself, and then I feel bad about not feeling like myself.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the mood symptoms are causing marked impairment beyond what is typical for an adjustment reaction, helping distinguish major depressive disorder from adjustment disorder.
doctor.question: Have these feelings made it hard for you to do your job or manage your usual responsibilities?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’m still making it to work, but my supervisor has already noticed incomplete charting, and I’ve been pulling away from friends and the things that usually keep me steady.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms are interfering with work or usual responsibilities, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yes… I think it has, even though I’m still showing up and doing my shifts. I haven’t called out or anything, and I keep telling myself that means I’m functioning, but it’s not the same as before.

At work, I’m getting through the day, but it takes so much more effort to stay on top of everything. My supervisor has already noticed that some of my charting hasn’t been finished the way it should be, which felt really embarrassing. I’m usually very careful about that, so having someone point it out made me feel like, okay, this isn’t just in my head. It’s actually affecting how I’m doing my job.

And outside of work, I’ve been pulling back a lot. Friends will text me and I’ll see it and think I should answer, and then I just… don’t. Or I put it off until it feels too awkward. I’m also not really doing the things that usually keep me steady, like staying connected with people or keeping up with my normal routines. I still manage the basic responsibilities, but it feels like I’m doing the bare minimum and slowly letting the rest slip.

doctor.intent: Determine whether she has had thoughts of death or suicide, a key major depressive episode symptom that would strongly support F32.9 over adjustment disorder and is important for safety assessment.
doctor.question: Have you had any thoughts about wanting to die or hurting yourself?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: What scared me enough to say something at my prenatal appointment was that I’ve been having thoughts like I wish I just wouldn’t wake up, even though I don’t have a plan to hurt myself.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about thoughts of wanting to die or self-harm, which corresponds to recurrent thoughts of death or suicidal ideation.

patient.answer:
Yeah… um… that’s actually the thing that scared me enough to say something at my prenatal appointment.

I haven’t made a plan to hurt myself, and I don’t have, like, a specific thing I’m going to do. But I’ve been having thoughts like… I wish I could just not wake up. Like if I went to sleep and somehow didn’t have to keep doing this, there’s a part of me that feels relieved by that thought, and that really scared me when I noticed it.

It’s hard to say out loud because I don’t want people to think I’m trying to do something or that I’m unsafe every second, but it also doesn’t feel okay to keep pretending it’s nothing. I haven’t been thinking, “I’m going to hurt myself,” exactly. It’s more like I don’t want to be here, or I want everything to stop, and then I feel awful and frightened that I’m even thinking that.

inference.note: Passive death wishes/suicidal ideation plus depressed mood, anhedonia, impaired concentration, and functional impairment support a current major depressive episode and increase severity to severe without psychotic symptoms (F32.2). Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.2) remains possible because symptoms began after discovering the pregnancy, but the syndrome appears more pervasive/intense than a simple stress reaction.

doctor.intent: Determine whether she has psychomotor retardation, which would help establish a major depressive episode over adjustment disorder.
doctor.question: Have you noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking more slowly than usual lately?

target_item.name: Psychomotor_Changes
target_item.manifestation: Everything I do feels slowed down, like I’m moving through syrup, and even simple things at the clinic like gathering wound supplies or finishing charting take me noticeably longer than they should.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about moving or speaking more slowly than usual, which directly corresponds to psychomotor changes.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. I didn’t really have words for it at first, but it feels like everything I do is slowed down, like I’m moving through syrup or something. Not just tired, exactly, but like my body takes longer to start and longer to finish anything.

At the clinic, even simple things that I normally do automatically feel like they take effort. Like gathering wound care supplies — that should be quick, I know where everything is — but I’ll find myself moving so slowly, double-checking, standing there for a second like I’m trying to remember the next step. And charting takes me noticeably longer than it should. I’ll be sitting there trying to finish something that used to feel routine, and it’s like my hands and my brain are both dragging.

I don’t know if other people would see it as me moving in slow motion or if it just feels that way to me, but I definitely notice that I’m not as quick or efficient as I usually am. It’s frustrating because I know how I normally function, and this is not that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive episode is pervasive and autonomous rather than primarily an emotional response centered on the identifiable stressor, to distinguish major depressive disorder from adjustment disorder.
doctor.question: When you’re occupied with something unrelated to the pregnancy, does the sadness still feel just as strong?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: I came in because for the past few weeks I’ve felt this heavy, sad pressure sitting on me almost all day, and even when I’m at work smiling at patients, inside I feel like I’m barely holding myself together.
target_item.reason: The question is asking whether the sad mood persists even when attention is on something unrelated, which directly relates to persistent depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah… it does. That’s part of what’s been confusing and honestly kind of scary to me. It’s not only when I’m thinking about the pregnancy or appointments or anything like that. Even when I’m busy with something completely separate, like work stuff, talking to a patient, trying to chart, or doing something that should distract me, it’s still there.

I can be smiling at a patient and saying the right things, and on the outside I probably look normal enough, but inside it feels like there’s this heavy, sad pressure just sitting on me almost all day. Like I’m having to hold myself together underneath everything I’m doing. Sometimes I’ll realize I’ve been going through the motions for hours, and the sadness hasn’t really lifted — I’ve just been trying to work around it.

That’s honestly why I came in. It’s been going on for the past few weeks, and it feels like it follows me into whatever I’m doing, not just when I’m focused on one specific worry.

inference.note: Symptoms meet a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms: depressed mood most of the day nearly every day, anhedonia, impaired concentration, psychomotor slowing, functional impairment, and passive death wishes. The sadness persists even when not thinking about the pregnancy and appears disproportionate to the stressor, making F43.2 less likely.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms: depressed mood most of the day nearly every day for over 2 weeks, marked loss of interest, impaired concentration, psychomotor retardation, passive thoughts of death, and clear occupational/social impairment. Although symptoms began after learning of pregnancy, the syndrome is more intense and pervasive than an expected stress reaction, persists even when not thinking about the pregnancy, and is not better explained by chronic depressive disorder.
